g.text: Figure 4d | Cue-aligned firing-rate prototypes for all 16 subtypes

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #56616f

g.text: Every prototype uses the same firing-rate axis, so response magnitudes and temporal motifs can be compared directly.

text.style: font-size: 6.45px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #56616f

g.text: The 16 subtype-average firing-rate traces share a single y-axis range and a common −1 to +5 s time axis. The dashed magenta line marks cue onset. These curves summarize functional response motifs from one recording and

text.style: font-size: 6.45px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #56616f

g.text: do not establish stable neuronal cell types.
